passages.text: Out of my distress, I called on Yah. Yah answered me with freedom. Yahweh is on my side. I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?
passages.note: Fear of others; finding freedom out of distress

passages.text: The stone which the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. This is Yahweh’s doing. It is marvelous in our eyes. This is the day that Yahweh has made. We will rejoice and be glad in it!
passages.note: Being rejected, then found essential; gladness in today

passages.text: I am a stranger on the earth. Don’t hide your commandments from me.
passages.note: Feeling like a stranger in the world

passages.text: My soul is weary with sorrow: strengthen me according to your word.
passages.note: Weariness from sorrow; asking for strength

passages.text: It is good for me that I have been afflicted, that I may learn your statutes.
I have seen a limit to all perfection, but your commands are boundless.
passages.note: The limits of perfection; letting go of perfectionism

passages.text: Your word is a lamp to my feet, and a light for my path.
passages.note: Guidance when unsure of the way forward

passages.text: I rise before dawn and cry for help. I put my hope in your words. My eyes stay open through the night watches, that I might meditate on your word.
passages.note: Sleepless nights; holding on to hope
